A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEMA, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C. The material supports reliable matching despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments on four datasets, component ablations, parameter-efficiency analyses, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds limited-data comparisons, training-time measurements, LoRA results, and repeated-run statistics.

M1.justification: v2 adds and evaluates LoRA as an alternative functional adapter, extending v1's AdaptFormer and Convpass implementations (Table 3). The default adapter architecture, representation descriptors, expansion strategy, and learned mixture router remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-incremental learning on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, and the same five-domain VTAB collection. v2's VTAB-1/2 and ImageNet-A 10%/20% experiments subsample retained datasets; they change sample budgets without adding datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds EASE as an evaluated comparator in the limited-data experiments (Appendix C.6, Tables 12–13). EASE's underlying paper was already cited in v1, but no EASE results were reported there. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation protocols through 90% data removal from one or two VTAB tasks, 10%/20% ImageNet-A retention, and per-batch training-time measurements. It also replaces the forced two-adapter VTAB control with automatic expansion restricted to the final layer. The retained benchmark splits, metrics, backbone weights, and stated training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds data-efficiency tests, a LoRA ablation, and robustness reporting across class orders and initializations. It replaces v1's ImageNet-A minimum-z-score illustration and two-adapter VTAB case with VTAB reconstruction-error and three-adapter usage analyses. Existing threshold, expansion-depth, and AE-width studies remain, with the AE-width study moved to Appendix C.8.

E5.justification: v1 provides no experimental run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 Appendix C.7 and Table 14 report SEMA means and standard deviations over five independent runs on all four datasets, varying class order and initialization. This establishes new uncertainty reporting, without establishing an increase over a specified v1 run count.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark, ablation, inference-time, and 10-task table values are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results on LoRA, training cost, and limited data. In Table 12, SEMA's final VTAB-1/2 accuracies are 81.33/80.06 versus EASE's 78.37/78.86. In Table 13, ImageNet-A 10%/20% results are 41.41/48.26 versus 41.67/48.65. Replaced expansion and routing illustrations use different controls, so they do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical substance of the adapter, routing, reconstruction loss, expansion score, and evaluation metrics is retained. v2's overall objective in Equation 4 consolidates the existing classification and reconstruction objectives. No new theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim rehearsal-free, demand-driven adapter expansion and learned composition that improve continual classification while reusing knowledge. v2 foregrounds stability–plasticity balance and sub-linear growth, but these ideas, including the explicit sub-linear-growth claim, were already present in v1, particularly Appendix C.2.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking limited-data performance and training efficiency to knowledge reuse and skipped expansion. Its router discussion emphasizes unreliable individual-sample descriptor decisions, while v1 emphasized the mismatch between descriptor and classification objectives. The limitations discussion expands the retained task-boundary restriction to discuss online learning, intra-task diversity, and improving descriptor-driven expansion.

D1.justification: v2 adds GPU information, separate adapter/descriptor timing, and parallel-execution guidance. It removes Algorithm 1, Appendix A.2's detailed batch-based expansion discussion and 500-sample statistics window, and the explicit default AE width of 128. Core optimization settings and baseline implementation links remain. These documentation differences do not establish corresponding changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 updates positioning against task-specific expansion and adds citations including variational autoencoders and mixture-of-experts adapters for vision-language continual learning. References such as Varigrow and Moduleformer disappear. Most related work remains; EASE was already cited, although v2 discusses its architecture and relationship to SEMA more extensively.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. v2 reorganizes the method around a separate overall-objective subsection, removes the pseudocode and dedicated expansion-score appendix, expands the limitations discussion, and relocates the AE-width analysis. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 substantially changes typography, margins, table placement, and figure arrangement, including converting retained four-panel plots into single rows. It replaces the expansion diagnostic and adapter-usage graphics, adds result tables, redisplays the existing parameter-growth plot in the main text, and moves the AE-width figure to the appendix.

improvement.justification: Five-run uncertainty reporting addresses v1's lack of experimental variability estimates, while training-time and limited-data comparisons make efficiency claims better assessable. These gains are tempered by removing the pseudocode and concrete expansion-statistics and AE-default details, which weakens reproducibility. With the principal benchmark findings unchanged, the evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
